subject: API dry-run: credential checks, sandbox access, and backup windows
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Green <matt.green@finstack.io>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: API dry-run: credential checks, sandbox access, and backup windows

Hi Matt —

Thanks again for booking the console + API onboarding next week. Before we run the full customer session (goal: feature walk-through + hands-on lab), I want to slot a short internal dry-run to validate:

- Sandbox credentials and scopes (API key vs. OAuth).
- SSO/JIT provisioning flow (if you plan to use IdP).
- Test prompts and the KV cache behavior on your sample traces.
- Timing for the hands-on lab (we recommend 60–75 mins total).

Would you and Priya be open to a 30–40 minute technical tryout the day before the public session? Proposed windows (your timezone):

- Tue 6/22 10:00–10:40 AM ET
- Tue 6/22 4:00–4:40 PM ET (backup)

If neither works, list two preferred windows and we’ll match. I’ve attached a short runbook and the sandbox access instructions.

Camila, can you confirm whether we need to rotate a demo API key ahead of the dry-run? Ben — can you standby for token-limit checks during the tryout (quick telemetry check only).

Thanks —
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0118

Attachments: dryrun-runbook-v1.pdf (7KB), sandbox-access-instructions.txt (2KB)
From: Matt Green <matt.green@finstack.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@optifin.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: API dry-run: credential checks, sandbox access, and backup windows

Thanks Sofia — that sounds perfect. Priya and I can do the 10:00 AM ET slot on 6/22. A couple of quick notes:

- Priya will bring a sample dataset and a short prompt list (~10 items) we want to run through.
- Our security team requires any external keys to be scoped to a sandbox project; Priya will share the expected scopes.
- We should test the redirect URI for our Okta integration during the tryout.

I'll send a calendar invite for 6/22 10:00 AM ET. Can you confirm the meeting length (30 vs 40 min)? Also dropping Camila a note to coordinate the key rotation.

—Matt
Matt Green
CTO, FinStack
matt.green@finstack.io

Subject: Re: API dry-run: credential checks, sandbox access, and backup windows

Sofia / Ben —

We can support the 6/22 10:00 AM ET (that’s 7:00 AM PT for me, fine). Notes from my side:

- I’ll provision a sandbox-scoped API key that expires after 48 hours and send it to Matt via secure share.
- For Okta redirect URIs, please use the test.okta.redwood redirect we reserve for partners — I’ll add that to the runbook.
- Ben: please stand by to validate token issuance and to watch for rate-limit warnings (I’ll include a short telemetry checklist below).

Telemetry checklist (short):
- Token metadata (scope, expiry)
- Per-second request rate during the prompt burst
- Any 5xx responses and full request/response IDs for triage

Sofia: I’ve attached the sandbox instructions with the redirect entry highlighted. I’ll drop the secure key link 30 minutes before the tryout.

—Camila

All good on my end — I’ll be on the call for the 10:00 AM ET tryout and will monitor:

- Token issuance logs (first 5 tokens)
- Per-region queue depth and latency spikes
- Any partial responses (we’ll capture request IDs)

One small ask: if FinStack plans a prompt burst >50 tokens per user, flag it in calendar notes so I can pre-warm the test runner.

Matt/Priya: when you accept the invite, please add the sample prompt doc to the calendar event (we’ll run them in order). If anything changes I’ll send an update.

Thanks —
